paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear two long conversations. At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions. Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A)，B)，C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将听到两个长对话。在每次对话结束时，您都会听到四个问题。对话和问题都只会说一次。听到问题后，您必须从标记为 A)，B)，C) 和 D) 的四个选项中选择最佳答案。然后在答卷 1 上用一条穿过中心的线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: The dream of personalised flight is still vivid in the minds of many inventors, some developing cycle-powered craft, others 26 money into jetpacks (喷气飞行背包). However, the flying car has always remained the 27 symbol of personal transport freedom.
paragraphs.translationZh: 个性化飞行的梦想在许多发明家的脑海中仍然清晰可见，一些人开发了自行车动力飞行器，另一些人则投入大量资金开发喷气背包。然而，飞行汽车始终是个人交通自由的终极象征。

paragraphs.sourceText: Several companies around the world have produced 28 that can drive on roads and fly. Airbus has a futuristic modular (组件式的) concept involving a passenger capsule that can be 29 from the road-going chassis (底盘) and picked up by a helicopter-type machine.
paragraphs.translationZh: 世界各地的几家公司已经生产了可以在道路上行驶和飞行的原型机。空中客车公司有一个未来的模块化（组件式）概念，涉及一个乘客舱，可以从公路底盘（成型）上拆卸下来，并由直升机型机器拾取。

paragraphs.sourceText: But all these concepts are massively expensive, require safety certification standards for road and air, need 30 controls, involve complex folding wings and propellers, and have to be flown from air-strips. So they are likely to remain rich people’s playthings rather than practical transport solutions for the masses.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但所有这些概念都非常昂贵，需要道路和空中安全认证标准，需要双重控制，涉及复杂的折叠机翼和螺旋桨，并且必须从机场起飞。因此，它们很可能仍然是富人的玩物，而不是大众的实用交通解决方案。

paragraphs.sourceText: “A car that takes off from some London street and lands in another 31 street is unlikely to happen,” says Prof. Gray, a leading aeronautical engineer. “Sky taxis are much more likely.” But that won’t stop inventors from dreaming up new ways to fly and trying to persuade investors to back their sometimes 32 schemes.
paragraphs.translationZh: “汽车从伦敦某条街道起飞并随机降落在另一条街道上的情况不太可能发生，”领先的航空工程师格雷教授说。 “空中出租车的可能性更大。”但这并不能阻止发明家梦想新的飞行方式，并试图说服投资者支持他们有时令人震惊的计划。

paragraphs.sourceText: Civilian aviation is being disrupted, not by the age-old desires for speed, romanticism and 33 , but by the pressing need to respond to a changing climate. New electric engines coupled with artificial intelligence and 34 systems will contribute to a more efficient, integrated transport system that is less polluting and less noisy. That may sound simple, but as Prof. Gray says, “When I travel somewhere I like this notion that when I finish my journey I feel better than when I started it. That’s completely at 35 with how I feel today.” Now that would be progress.
paragraphs.translationZh: 民用航空正在受到干扰，不是因为对速度、浪漫主义和魅力的古老渴望，而是因为应对气候变化的迫切需要。新型电动发动机与人工智能和自主系统相结合，将有助于打造更高效、污染更少、噪音更低的综合运输系统。这听起来可能很简单，但正如格雷教授所说，“当我去某个地方旅行时，我喜欢这样的想法：当我完成旅程时，我感觉比开始时更好。这与我今天的感受完全不一致。”现在这将是进步。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Companies Are Working with Consumers to Reduce Waste
paragraphs.translationZh: 公司正在与消费者合作减少浪费

paragraphs.sourceText: A) As consumers, we are very wasteful. Annually, the world generates 1.3 billion tons of solid waste. This is expected to go up to 2.2 billion by 2025. The developed countries are responsible for 44% of waste, and in the U.S. alone, the average person throws away their body weight in rubbish every month.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 作为消费者，我们非常浪费。全球每年产生 13 亿吨固体废物。预计到 2025 年，这一数字将达到 22 亿。发达国家造成了 44% 的垃圾，仅在美国，平均每个人每月都会将与自身体重相当的垃圾扔掉。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Conventional wisdom would seem to suggest that companies have no incentive to lengthen the life cycle of their products and reduce the revenue they would get from selling new goods. Yet, more and more businesses are thinking about how to reduce consumer waste. This is partly driven by the rising price of raw materials and metals. It is also partly due to both consumers and companies becoming more aware of the need to protect our environment.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 传统观点似乎表明，公司没有动力延长产品的生命周期并减少销售新产品的收入。然而，越来越多的企业正在考虑如何减少消费者浪费。这在一定程度上是由原材料和金属价格上涨推动的。部分原因是消费者和公司都越来越意识到保护环境的必要性。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) When choosing what products to buy and which brands to buy from, more and more consumers are looking into sustainability. This is opposed to just price and performance they were concerned about in the past. In a survey of 54 of the world’s leading brands, almost all of them reported that consumers are showing increasing care about sustainable lifestyles. At the same time, surveys on consumers in the U.S. and the U.K. show that they also care about minimizing energy use and reducing waste.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 在选择购买什么产品和购买哪些品牌时，越来越多的消费者开始关注可持续性。这与他们过去只关心价格和性能相反。在对 54 个全球领先品牌的调查中，几乎所有品牌都表示消费者越来越关心可持续的生活方式。与此同时，对美国和英国消费者的调查显示，他们也关心最大限度地减少能源使用和减少浪费。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) For the most part, consumers control what happens to a product. But some companies are realizing that placing the burden of recycling entirely on the consumer is not an effective strategy, especially when tossing something away seems like the easiest and most convenient option.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 在大多数情况下，消费者控制着产品发生的情况。但一些公司意识到，将回收的负担完全交给消费者并不是一个有效的策略，特别是当扔掉一些东西似乎是最简单、最方便的选择时。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Some retailers and manufacturers in the clothing, footwear, and electronics industries have launched environmental programs. They want to make their customers interested in preserving their products and preventing things that still have value from going to the garbage dump. By offering services to help expand the longevity of their products, they’re promising quality and durability to consumers, and receiving the reputational gains for being environmentally friendly.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 服装、鞋类和电子行业的一些零售商和制造商已经启动了环保计划。他们希望让客户有兴趣保存他们的产品并防止仍然有价值的东西进入垃圾场。通过提供有助于延长产品使用寿命的服务，他们向消费者承诺质量和耐用性，并因环保而赢得声誉。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) For example, the Swedish jeans company Nudie Jeans offers free repair at twenty of their shops. Instead of discarding their old worn-out jeans, customers bring them in to be renewed. The company even provides mail-order repair kits and online videos, so that customers can learn how to fix a pair of jeans at home. Their philosophy is that extending the life of a pair of jeans is not only great for the environment, but allows the consumer to get more value out of their product. When customers do want to toss their pair, they can give them back to the store, which will repurpose and resell them. Another clothing company, Patagonia, a high-end outdoor clothing store, follows the same principle. It has partnered with DIY website iFixit to teach consumers how to repair their clothing, such as waterproof outerwear, at home. The company also offers a repair program for their customers for a modest fee. Currently, Patagonia repairs about 40,000 garments a year in their Reno, Nevada, service center. According to the company’s CEO, Rose Marcario, this is about building a company that cares about the environment. At the same time, offering repair supports the perceived quality of its products.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 例如，瑞典牛仔裤公司 Nudie Jeans 在其 20 家商店提供免费维修服务。顾客不会扔掉旧的破旧牛仔裤，而是把它们拿来翻新。该公司甚至提供邮购修理套件和在线视频，以便顾客可以学习如何在家修理牛仔裤。他们的理念是，延长牛仔裤的使用寿命不仅有利于环境，而且可以让消费者从产品中获得更多价值。当顾客确实想扔掉他们的鞋子时，他们可以将其退还给商店，商店将重新利用并转售它们。另一家服装公司巴塔哥尼亚（Patagonia）是一家高端户外服装店，也遵循同样的原则。它与 DIY 网站 iFixit 合作，教消费者如何在家修理防水外套等衣物。该公司还为客户提供维修计划，费用适中。目前，巴塔哥尼亚在内华达州里诺的服务中心每年修理约 40,000 件衣服。该公司首席执行官 Rose Marcario 表示，这是为了建立一家关心环境的公司。与此同时，提供维修服务也支持了其产品的感知质量。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) In Brazil, the multinational corporation Adidas has been running a shoe-recycling program called “Sustainable Footprint” since 2012. Customers can bring shoes of any brand into an Adidas store to be shredded and turned into alternative fuels for energy creation instead of being burned as trash. They are used to fuel cement ovens. To motivate visitors to bring in more old shoes, Adidas Brazil promotes the program in stores by showing videos to educate customers, and it even offers a discount each time a customer brings in an old pair of shoes. This boosts the reputation and image of Adidas by making people more aware of the company’s values.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 在巴西，跨国公司阿迪达斯自 2012 年以来一直在运行一项名为“可持续足迹”的鞋子回收计划。顾客可以将任何品牌的鞋子带到阿迪达斯商店，将其粉碎并转化为替代能源以产生能源，而不是作为垃圾焚烧。它们被用来为水泥炉提供燃料。为了鼓励游客引进更多旧鞋，阿迪达斯巴西公司在商店里通过播放视频来宣传该计划，以教育顾客，甚至每次顾客引进一双旧鞋时都会提供折扣。这使人们更加了解公司的价值观，从而提高了阿迪达斯的声誉和形象。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Enormous opportunities also lie with e-waste. It is estimated that in 2014 the world produced some 42 million metric tons of e-waste (discarded electrical and electronic equipment and its parts) with North America and Europe accounting for 8 and 12 million metric tons respectively. The materials from e-waste include iron, copper, gold, silver, and aluminum—materials that could be reused, resold, salvaged, or recycled. Together, the value of these metals is estimated to be about $52 billion. Electronics giants like Best Buy and Samsung have provided e-waste take-back programs over the past few years, which aim to refurbish (翻新) old electronic components and parts into new products.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 电子垃圾也蕴藏着巨大的机会。据估计，2014年全球产生了约4200万吨电子垃圾（废弃的电气和电子设备及其零部件），其中北美和欧洲分别占8和1200万吨。电子垃圾中的材料包括铁、铜、金、银和铝，这些材料可以重复使用、转售、回收或回收。这些金属的总价值估计约为 520 亿美元。过去几年，百思买和三星等电子巨头推出了电子垃圾回收计划，旨在将旧电子元器件翻新成新产品。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) For other companies interested in reducing waste, helping the environment, and providing the sustainable lifestyles that consumers seek, here are some first steps for building a relationship with customers that focuses on recycling and restoring value to products:
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 对于其他对减少浪费、保护环境和提供消费者寻求的可持续生活方式感兴趣的公司，以下是与客户建立关系的一些初步步骤，重点是回收和恢复产品价值：

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Find partners. If you are a manufacturer who relies on outside distributors, then retailers are the ideal partner for collecting old products. Power tool maker DeWalt partners with companies, such as Lowes and Napa Auto Parts, to collect old tools at their stores for recycling. The partnership benefits both sides by allowing unconventional partners (for example, two companies from two different industries) to work together on a specific aspect of the value chain, like, in this example, an engine firm with an accessory one.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 寻找合作伙伴。如果您是一家依赖外部分销商的制造商，那么零售商是收集旧产品的理想合作伙伴。电动工具制造商 DeWalt 与 Lowes 和 Napa Auto Parts 等公司合作，在其商店收集旧工具进行回收。这种伙伴关系使双方都受益，因为它允许非常规合作伙伴（例如，来自两个不同行业的两家公司）在价值链的特定方面进行合作，例如本例中的发动机公司和配件公司。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Create incentives. Environmental conscientiousness isn’t always enough to make customers recycle old goods. For instance, DeWalt discovered that many contractors were holding on to their old tools, even if they no longer worked, because they were expensive purchases and it was hard to justify bringing them in to recycle. By offering instant discounts worth as much as $100, DeWalt launched a trade-in program to encourage people to bring back tools. As a result, DeWalt now reuses those materials to create new products.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 制定激励措施。环境责任感并不总是足以让顾客回收旧货。例如，德瓦尔特发现许多承包商保留着他们的旧工具，即使它们不再工作，因为它们的购买成本很高，而且很难证明将它们回收利用是合理的。通过提供高达 100 美元的即时折扣，DeWalt 推出了一项以旧换新计划，鼓励人们带回工具。因此，得伟现在重复利用这些材料来创造新产品。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Start with a trial program, and expect to change the details as you go. Any take-back program will likely change over time, depending on what works for your customers and company goals. Maybe you see low customer participation at first, or conversely, so much success that the cost of recycling becomes too high. Best Buy, for instance, has been bearing the lion’s share of e-waste volume since two of its largest competitors, Amazon and Wal-mart, do not have their own recycling programs. Since the launch of its program, Best Buy changed its policy to add a $25 fee for recycling old televisions in order to keep the program going.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 从试用计划开始，并期望在实施过程中更改细节。任何回收计划都可能会随着时间的推移而改变，具体取决于什么对您的客户和公司目标有效。也许您一开始看到客户参与度较低，或者相反，由于取得了巨大的成功，回收成本变得过高。例如，百思买一直承担着电子垃圾量的最大份额，因为其最大的两个竞争对手亚马逊和沃尔玛没有自己的回收计划。自该计划启动以来，百思买改变了政策，对旧电视回收收取 25 美元的费用，以保持该计划的继续进行。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Build a culture of collective values with customers. A stronger relationship between the retailer/producer and the consumer isn’t just about financial incentives. By creating more awareness around your efforts to reduce waste, and by developing a culture of responsibility, repair, and reuse, you can build customer loyalty based on shared values and responsibilities.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 与客户一起建立集体价值观的文化。零售商/生产商与消费者之间更牢固的关系不仅仅是经济激励。通过提高人们对减少浪费的努力的认识，并发展责任、维修和再利用的文化，您可以在共同的价值观和责任的基础上建立客户忠诚度。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) These examples are just the tip of the iceberg, but they demonstrate how helping customers get more use of their materials can transform value chains and operations. Reducing waste by incorporating used materials into production can cut costs and decrease the price of procurement (采购): less to be procured from the outside and more to be re-utilized from the inside.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 这些例子只是冰山一角，但它们展示了如何帮助客户更多地利用他们的材料可以改变价值链和运营。通过将废旧材料纳入生产来减少浪费，可以降低成本并降低采购价格：从外部采购的材料更少，从内部重新利用的材料更多。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Companies play a big role in creating a circular economy, in which value is generating less from extracting new resources and more from getting better use out of the resources we already have—but they must also get customers engaged in the process.
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 公司在创建循环经济方面发挥着重要作用，在这种经济中，通过提取新资源产生的价值越来越少，而通过更好地利用我们现有的资源产生的价值却越来越多，但他们也必须让客户参与到这一过程中。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Some companies believe that products’ prolonged lifespan benefits both the environment and customers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 一些公司认为，延长产品的使用寿命对环境和客户都有好处。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. A survey shows shoppers today are getting more concerned about energy conservation and environmental protection when deciding what to buy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 一项调查显示，当今的购物者在决定购买什么产品时越来越关注节能和环保。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Companies can build customer loyalty by creating a positive culture of environmental awareness.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 公司可以通过营造积极的环境意识文化来建立客户忠诚度。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. When companies launch environmental programs, they will have their brand reputation enhanced.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 当公司推出环保计划时，他们的品牌声誉将会提高。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. One multinational company offers discounts to customers who bring in old footwear to be used as fuel.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 一家跨国公司向购买旧鞋用作燃料的顾客提供折扣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Recycling used products can help manufacturers reduce production costs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 回收旧产品可以帮助制造商降低生产成本。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Electronic products contain valuable metals that could be recovered.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 电子产品含有可回收的贵重金属。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Effective Friday, Screen Actors Guild-American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (SAG-AFTRA) has declared a strike against 11 video game publishers over games that went into production after Feb. 17, 2015. The companies include some of the heavyweights of the industry, like Electronic Arts Productions, Insomniac Games, Activision and Disney.
paragraphs.translationZh: 自周五起，美国演员工会-美国电视和广播艺术家联合会 (SAG-AFTRA) 宣布对 11 家视频游戏发行商发起罢工，要求其停止制作 2015 年 2 月 17 日之后制作的游戏。这些公司包括一些业内重量级公司，如 Electronic Arts Productions、Insomniac Games、Activision 和 Disney。

paragraphs.sourceText: The strike comes in light of an unsuccessful 19 months of negotiations after the existing labor contract known as the Interactive Media Agreement expired in late 2014. overall, the strike is an effort to provide more secondary compensation along with other concerns, such as transparency upon hiring talent and on-set ( 制作中) safety precautions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这次罢工是在现有的劳动合同（即“互动媒体协议”）于 2014 年底到期后，历时 19 个月的谈判未能成功而发生的。总体而言，这次罢工是为了提供更多的次要补偿，同时也考虑到其他问题，例如招聘人才的透明度和现场安全预防措施。

paragraphs.sourceText: The video gaming industry has ballooned in recent years. The Los Angeles Times reports that the industry is in the midst of an intense increase in cash flow. In 2015, gaming produced $23.5 billion in domestic revenue.
paragraphs.translationZh: 近年来，视频游戏行业蓬勃发展。据《洛杉矶时报》报道，该行业正处于现金流的急剧增长之中。 2015 年，游戏在国内创造了 235 亿美元的收入。

paragraphs.sourceText: But SAG-AFTRA says voice actors don’t receive residuals (追加酬金) for their gaming work. Instead, they receive a fixed rate, which is typically about $825 for a standard four-hour vocal session. So the voice actors are pushing for the idea of secondary compensation—a performance bonus every time a game sells 2 million copies or downloads, or reaches 2 million subscribers, with a cap at 8 million.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但 SAG-AFTRA 表示，配音演员不会因其游戏工作而获得额外报酬金。相反，他们会收到固定费率，通常四小时标准声乐课程的费用约为 825 美元。因此，配音演员们正在推动二次补偿的想法——每当游戏销量达到 200 万份或下载量，或者达到 200 万订阅者时，就会获得绩效奖金，上限为 800 万。

paragraphs.sourceText: “It’s a very small number of games that would trigger this secondary compensation issue,” said voice actor Crispin Freeman, who’s a member of the union’s negotiating committee. “This is an important aspect of what it means to be a freelance (从事自由职业的) performer, who isn’t regularly employed every single day working on projects.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 工会谈判委员会成员、配音演员克里斯平·弗里曼 (Crispin Freeman) 表示：“只有极少数游戏会引发次要补偿问题。” “这是成为一名自由职业者的一个重要方面，他们并不是每天都定期从事项目工作。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Another major complaint from the actors is the secrecy of the industry. “I can’t imagine if there’s any other acting job in the world where you don’t know what show you’re in, when you’re hired,”says voice actor Keythe Farley, who chairs the SAG-AFTRA negotiating committee.
paragraphs.translationZh: 演员们的另一个主要抱怨是行业的保密性。 “我无法想象世界上是否还有其他演艺工作，当你被录用时，你不知道自己在演什么节目，”美国演员工会和美国电视交易协会谈判委员会主席、配音演员凯斯·法利说道。

paragraphs.sourceText: “And yet that happens every day in the video game world,”Farley told reporters during a press conference Friday. “I was a main character in Fallout 4, a character by the name of Kellogg, and I never knew that I was doing vocal recording for that game throughout the year and a half.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “然而，这种情况在电子游戏世界中每天都会发生，”法利在周五的新闻发布会上告诉记者。 “我是《辐射 4》中的主角，一个名叫凯洛格的角色，我从来不知道自己在这一年半的时间里为这款游戏录制了声音。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Scott Witlin, the lawyer representing the video game companies, says voice actors “represent less than one tenth of 1 percent of the work that goes into making a video game.” So “even though they’re the top craftsmen in their field,”Witlin says, “if we pay them under a vastly different system than the people who do the 99.9 percent of the work, that’s going to create far more problems for the video game companies.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 视频游戏公司的代理律师斯科特·威特林 (Scott Witlin) 表示，配音演员“只占视频游戏制作工作量的不到百分之一的十分之一”。因此，“即使他们是各自领域的顶尖工匠，”威特林说，“如果我们按照与完成 99.9% 工作的人截然不同的制度支付他们工资，这将为视频游戏公司带来更多问题。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Officials at the White House announced a new space policy focused on managing the increasing number of satellites that companies and governments are launching into space. Space Policy Directive-3 lays out general guidelines for the United States to mitigate (缓解) the effects of space debris and track and manage traffic in space.
paragraphs.translationZh: 白宫官员宣布了一项新的太空政策，重点是管理公司和政府向太空发射的越来越多的卫星。太空政策指令 3 为美国减轻太空碎片的影响以及跟踪和管理太空交通制定了一般准则。

paragraphs.sourceText: This policy sets the stage for the Department of Commerce to take over the management of traffic in space. The department will make sure that newly launched satellites don’t use radio frequencies that would interfere with existing satellites, and schedule when such new satellites can be launched. This only applies to American space activities, but the hope is that it will help standardize a set of norms in the dawning commercial spaceflight industry throughout the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这项政策为商务部接管太空交通管理奠定了基础。该部门将确保新发射的卫星不使用会干扰现有卫星的无线电频率，并安排何时发射此类新卫星。这仅适用于美国的太空活动，但希望它将有助于在全球范围内新兴的商业航天工业中标准化一套规范。

paragraphs.sourceText: Space, especially the space directly around our planet, is getting more crowded as more governments and companies launch satellites. One impetus for the policy is that companies are already starting to build massive constellations (星座), comprising hundreds or thousands of satellites with many moving parts among them. With so much stuff in space, and a limited area around our planet, the government wants to reduce the chances of a collision. Two or more satellites slamming into each other could create many more out-of-control bits that would pose even more hazards to the growing collection of satellites in space.
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着越来越多的政府和公司发射卫星，太空，尤其是地球周围的空间变得越来越拥挤。该政策的推动力之一是，公司已经开始建造大型星座（星座），其中包括数百或数千颗卫星，其中有许多移动部件。太空中有如此多的东西，而地球周围的区域却有限，政府希望减少碰撞的可能性。两颗或更多卫星相互撞击可能会产生更多失控的碎片，这将对太空中不断增加的卫星造成更大的危害。

paragraphs.sourceText: And it’s not like this hasn’t happened before. In 2009 an old Russian craft slammed into a communications satellite, creating a cloud of hundreds of pieces of debris and putting other hardware at risk. Journalist Sarah Scoles reports that NASA currently tracks about 24,000 objects in space, and in 2016 the Air Force had to issue 3,995,874 warnings to satellite owners alerting them to a potential nearby threat from another satellite or bit of debris.
paragraphs.translationZh: 而且这种事以前也不是没有发生过。 2009 年，一艘俄罗斯旧飞船撞上了一颗通信卫星，形成了由数百块碎片组成的云，并使其他硬件面临风险。记者 Sarah Scoles 报道称，NASA 目前正在追踪太空中约 24,000 个物体，2016 年，空军不得不向卫星所有者发出 3,995,874 条警告，提醒他们注意附近来自另一颗卫星或碎片的潜在威胁。

paragraphs.sourceText: That’s why this new policy also includes directions to update the current U.S. Government Orbital Debris Mitigation Standard Practices, which already require any entity that launches a satellite or spacecraft to vigorously analyze the likelihood that any of their actions, from an unexpected failure or normal operations, will create more space debris. It includes accounting for any piece of debris they plan to release over 5mm that might stay in orbit for 25 years or more. It might seem surprising to think about an item staying in space for that long, but the oldest satellite still in orbit—Vanguard 1—turned 60 in 2018.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，这项新政策还包括更新当前美国政府轨道碎片减缓标准实践的指示，该实践已经要求任何发射卫星或航天器的实体积极分析其任何行动（由于意外故障或正常操作）将产生更多空间碎片的可能性。其中包括计算他们计划释放的任何超过 5 毫米的碎片，这些碎片可能会在轨道上停留 25 年或更长时间。一个物体在太空中停留这么长时间似乎令人惊讶，但仍在轨道上最古老的卫星——先锋 1 号——已于 2018 年满 60 岁了。

paragraphs.sourceText: Agencies and companies throughout the world are working on developing technology that would dispose of or capture space debris before it causes serious damage. But for now, the U.S. government is more focused on preventing new debris from forming than taking the trash out of orbit.
paragraphs.translationZh: 世界各地的机构和公司正在致力于开发能够在空间碎片造成严重损害之前处理或捕获空间碎片的技术。但目前，美国政府更关注的是防止新碎片的形成，而不是将垃圾带出轨道。
